newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu vows to keep tunnel open.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu vows to keep tunnel open.

text.p: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Saturday that Israel would never close a tunnel in Jerusalem which triggered Palestinian protests threatening Middle East peace.
"The tunnel has been around for 2,000 years... It will stay open. It will always be open," he said in a speech to 6,000 cheering Christian supporters of Israel from abroad.

Israeli workmen last week punched a new entrance in the tunnel, an archaeological tourist site, drawing international condemnation and triggering the protests by Palestinians who called it an assault on nearby Islamic shrines.
"This tunnel is 250 metres, a quarter of a km, from the nearest mosque... We believe in the freedom of all three great faiths... That was, is and will always remain our policy," he said.
Netanyahu said Israel had been subjected to "libelous slander" by those who said the tunnel threatened holy sites. This was "utter fabrication," he said.
The Palestinian actions "to incite religious war" were "unpardonable" and "irresponsible," he said.

Palestinian police kept a lid on protests in most of the West Bank and Gaza on Saturday while U.S. and U.N. officials tried to fix a PLO-Israeli summit to stop the violence which has claimed nearly 70 lives in the last four days.
Netanyahu's spokesman Shai Bazak said the Israeli leader was ready in principle to meet Palestinian President Yasser Arafat but: "For the moment there are no specific plans for a meeting."
Arafat will not meet Netanyahu alone without a prior guarantee that the tunnel entrance will be sealed. The tunnel is scheduled to reopen on Sunday after the Jewish sabbath.
"Our demands are clear. We want them to close the tunnel, put the peace process back on track, and immediately implement the Oslo accords," Arafat's aide Nabil Abu Rdainah said earlier.
Netanyahu has accused Arafat of "cynically" exploiting the tunnel issue and instigating the violence.
"It does not speak well of the international community that it accepts this violence...as a legitimate means of negotiation...We go towards the path of peace in peace," Netanyahu told the crowd.

"Thank you dear Christian friends...It's good to see you here in the eternal capital, undivided, of the Jewish people," Netanyahu said in a reference to Jerusalem, the eastern sector of which Israel captured in 1967 Middle East war and annexed.
Palestinians view East Jerusalem as the capital of a future independent state.
